counterexample: Converse direction is false under the proof's own conventions: let G be the 2-cycle on {u,v} with edges u->v and v->u. Since paths have positive length, GT = {(u,v),(v,u),(u,u),(v,v)}. No 1-edge graph on {u,v} has that closure, and among 2-edge graphs only F = {u->v, v->u} does (a self-loop at u cannot generate (v,u)), so G's transitive reduction is unique while G is cyclic. A single vertex with a self-loop is an even smaller counterexample. Hence 'unique transitive reduction => acyclic' fails as stated, and the proof never addresses this direction at all.
reasoning_summary:
Step-by-step verification of every numbered line.
0001 'Solution:' header - no mathematical content, nothing to justify.
0002-0003 Verbatim restatement of the definition of the transitive closure GT - faithful to the problem, justified.
0004-0005 Verbatim restatement of the definition of transitive reduction (minimum-edge graph with the same closure) - faithful, justified.
0006-0007 Verbatim restatement of the goal (unique transitive reduction iff acyclic) - justified as a statement of what must be proved.
0008 'Solution.' header - no content.
0009-0011 Conventions: finite digraphs, no parallel edges, directed paths of positive length. Legitimate to fix conventions; note the positive-length convention makes reachability irreflexive on a DAG and makes GT contain loops whenever G has a cycle - consistent so far, but it is exactly this convention that later dooms the unproved converse.
0012-0013 Formal definition of ET as the reachability relation - matches the problem's definition, justified.
0014-0015 Formal definition of a transitive reduction H = (V,F) with minimum |F| and HT = GT - matches the problem, justified.
0016 Announcement that the acyclic (classical) half comes first - organizational, acceptable.
0017 Theorem 1: if G is acyclic then G has a unique transitive reduction. This is the true standard result (the Hasse diagram); statement is legitimate, its proof must still be checked.
0018 'Proof.' plus the assertion that in a DAG the reachability relation is to be considered - opening move is appropriate.
0019-0021 Definition of u <= v as 'there is a directed path u ~> v' - well-defined given 0009-0011.
0022 Asserts this relation is a partial order on V. Justified in substance for a finite DAG (transitive by concatenation of paths; antisymmetric/irreflexive because a cycle would otherwise arise), though under the positive-length convention it is strictly a STRICT partial order, not a reflexive one. Minor terminological slip only; it does not break the argument since the cover relation is defined from the strict order.
0023-0025 Definition of the cover relation u <. v (u < v with no strictly intermediate w) - standard and well-defined, justified.
0026 Definition of the Hasse diagram H as the digraph of cover pairs - well-defined, justified.
0027-0029 Claim HT = GT, cited as a standard fact about posets. True for FINITE posets (finiteness is essential and is in force by 0009), so acceptable as an appeal to a standard result, though the finiteness dependence is left implicit.
0030 FIRST FAILING STEP. It announces 'We claim H is the unique transitive reduction. First, minimality:' and then argues only that no single edge of H can be deleted. Irredundancy (no edge removable) does not establish that H has the MINIMUM number of edges among all digraphs H' with H'T = GT, which is what the definition in 0014-0015 requires; a priori some entirely different, smaller edge set could have the same closure. The needed argument - that every H' with H'T = GT must contain each cover edge (u,v), since a witnessing path of length >= 2 would produce an intermediate w with u < w < v - is not given, and it is also precisely the argument that would deliver uniqueness. So the claim asserted at 0030 is not supported by what follows it.
0031-0032 The deletion argument itself is locally valid: any u->v path in H - (u,v) has length >= 2 and yields w with u < w < v, contradicting that (u,v) is a cover. Sound, but it only proves irredundancy, so it does not repair the gap opened at 0030.
0033 Line reads 'contradicting' followed by the page marker '1'; the text terminates mid-sentence. Consequently (a) the minimality argument is not finished, (b) the uniqueness half of Theorem 1 is never argued at all, and (c) the converse direction of the iff - unique transitive reduction implies acyclic - is never even begun.
Overall: the proof establishes at most that the Hasse diagram of a DAG has the right closure and no removable edge. It fails at 0030 (minimum-cardinality conflated with irredundancy), never proves uniqueness, and never proves the converse - which, under the proof's own positive-length path convention, is in fact false (see counterexample). Verdict: INVALID.
